stem: A keyboard user navigates into an interactive calendar widget but cannot move focus out of it using standard keyboard navigation keys. What accessibility failure does this illustrate?

options.rationale: A bypass mechanism lets users skip blocks of repeated content; it does not make a widget release keyboard focus.
A shortcut conflict occurs when a single-key shortcut blocks a character the user needs to type, not when focus cannot leave a component.
A control that needs a pointing device cannot be operated from the keyboard, whereas this widget accepts keyboard input and holds focus.
A keyboard trap occurs when keyboard focus enters an interface element but cannot exit using standard keys (such as Tab or Escape).

explanation: A keyboard trap is a critical accessibility barrier where a keyboard user can navigate into an interactive element (such as a modal window, popup, or calendar picker) but cannot navigate away using standard keystrokes. WCAG Success Criterion 2.1.2 explicitly prohibits keyboard traps.

references.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1: Success Criterion 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap
